proof.text: For each affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $Y$, [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] gives an affine open cover $h^{-1}(V)=\bigcup_j U_{V,j}$, with $U_{V,j}=\operatorname{Spec}A_{V,j}$ and $A_{V,j}$ a finite type $R$-algebra. The affine opens $V$ cover $Y$ by the definition of a scheme [def-pc-scheme], so all the $U_{V,j}$ together cover $X$. The hypothesis on $Y$ and [def-exc-excellent-ring] say that every such $R$ is Noetherian, a G-ring, and J-2. No finite cover of $Y$ or quasi-compactness of $h$ has been used.

proof.text: Fix a chart $R\to A=A_{V,j}$ from Step 1. Its finite type hypothesis and the Noetherianity of $R$ meet exactly the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], so $A$ is Noetherian. Since $R$ is a G-ring, apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-g-ring] to the same map to obtain that $A$ is a G-ring. Neither theorem requires $R\to A$ to be injective or $R$ to be universally catenary.

proof.text: The same $A$ is J-2 directly from the definitions. Indeed, let $C$ be any finite type $A$-algebra. Choose finitely many $R$-algebra generators $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ of $A$ and finitely many $A$-algebra generators $c_1,\ldots,c_s$ of $C$, using [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Expressing each coefficient from $A$ as a polynomial in the $a_i$ shows that the images of the $a_i$ together with the $c_j$ generate $C$ over $R$. Thus $C$ is a finite type $R$-algebra, and J-2 for $R$ says its regular locus is open. As this holds for every $C$, [def-exc-excellent-ring] gives J-2 for $A$. This is the finite type J-2 argument of Tag 07QU, with the composition of generators written out.

proof.text: The affine cover of Step 1 has Noetherian coordinate rings by Step 2. Hence $X$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Apply [lem-trf-g-ring-affine-cover] to this cover and its G-rings from Step 2: every affine open $W\subseteq X$ has a G-ring $B=\mathcal O_X(W)$. In particular $B$ is Noetherian, since this is part of [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Now [lem-trf-j2-affine-cover] applies to the same cover: its required local Noetherianity has just been established, and its charts are J-2 by Step 3. Thus every such $B$ is also J-2. These cover-locality statements apply to arbitrary schemes and arbitrary affine covers; no separatedness, finiteness of the cover, or assumption that intersections of affine opens are affine is needed.

proof.text: For every affine open $W\subseteq X$, Step 4 gives precisely Noetherianity, the G-ring property and J-2 for $\mathcal O_X(W)$. By [def-exc-excellent-ring] these three conditions say that its coordinate ring is quasi-excellent. This proves the first conclusion. Universal catenarity is an additional condition only for excellence, and has not been asserted or used; no bound on dimension was used.

If $X$ is quasi-compact, apply [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] to the affine open cover of Step 1 to choose a finite subcover $U_1,\ldots,U_m$. Every coordinate ring of this subcover is Noetherian by Step 2. This is exactly the finite affine cover condition for Noetherianness written in the statement (equivalently, local Noetherianity together with quasi-compactness, properties.tex Tag 01OV). If $X$ is empty, take the empty finite cover. Quasi-compactness is used only in this final step.

title: Quasi-excellence is preserved by locally finite-type morphisms
statement: Let $h:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume that every affine open of $Y$ has quasi-excellent coordinate ring [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Then every affine open of $X$ has quasi-excellent coordinate ring as well. If $X$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], then $X$ is Noetherian: it has a finite affine open cover whose coordinate rings are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. No finite-dimensionality or universal catenarity hypothesis is imposed.
